key_claims: Impaired glucose tolerance arises at 12 months of age in Wistar rats before detectable changes in body composition, circulating damage markers, or muscle mass.
Structural loss in muscle is preceded by functional and organizational decline between 15 and 18 months.

Early supplementation with n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids initiated at midlife significantly improved glucose tolerance, reduced adiposity, and enhanced neuromuscular performance without increasing muscle mass.
Functional benefits were paralleled by reduced markers of muscle damage and attenuation of histopathological alterations.
A substantial fraction of benefits persisted after cessation of supplementation, with animals displaying sustained metabolic and structural advantages at 18 months compared to age-matched controls.
limitations: The study was conducted in Wistar rats, not humans.
The exact duration and dosage of n-3 supplementation are not specified in the provided text.
The long-term effects beyond 18 months are not described.
The study does not provide mechanistic details on how n-3 supplementation exerts its effects.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that n-3 supplementation prevents muscle aging in humans.
The study shows that n-3 supplementation increases muscle mass.
The study identifies a specific molecular pathway for the benefits.
The study indicates that n-3 supplementation is effective at any age.
The study provides clinical recommendations for n-3 supplementation.
